headline: Butterfly Brought Back From the Brink of Extinction
meta_description: After dwindling to just 9 known individuals in the US, the Poweshiek skipperling butterfly is being restored through captive breeding and release.
summary_short: A rare butterfly species teetering on extinction is getting a second chance. Researchers released over 1,300 captive-raised Poweshiek skipperlings in 2025.
body:
The Poweshiek skipperling butterfly, once down to just 9 known individuals in the United States in 2022, is being brought back from the brink of extinction. Researchers have released more than 1,300 captive-raised butterflies into the wild in 2025, marking a significant milestone in species recovery.

The dramatic turnaround reflects years of dedicated conservation work. By breeding these delicate butterflies in controlled settings, scientists have managed to increase the population far beyond the critically low numbers recorded just three years earlier. The 2025 releases represent a carefully planned effort to restore the species to sustainable wild populations.

This recovery demonstrates how targeted intervention can save species from disappearing entirely. The Poweshiek skipperling's journey from the edge of extinction to a growing population offers hope for other endangered butterflies and insects facing similar threats.
quick_facts: Only 9 Poweshiek skipperlings known in the US in 2022
More than 1,300 captive-raised butterflies released in 2025
Species brought back from brink of extinction through breeding program
